warnings.title: E6 Set_Lane guard: auto-pipe zero-check is structurally dead and qos_auto_weights_after duplicates the ladder walk (~40 lines)
warnings.detail: qos_auto_weights_after unconditionally marks the candidate lane in-play and the catalog loader forces every ladder row entry into 1..MAX_WEIGHT (catalog.odin:1047-1050), so w[c.lane]==0 is unreachable on auto pipes — the promised E6 bus rejection cannot fire there (intended per comments, but the branch is dead code). The override scan + never-drop fold + ladder hand-out are duplicated from qos_auto_weights; the `class` parameter is never read. Blind also notes the fold resolves pre-edit overrides (a moved never-drop class reserves its old lane) — benign while the check is only ==0.
warnings.recommended_fix: Factor the shared in-play scan + fold + ladder walk into one internal helper parameterized by an optional candidate override; drop the unused `class` param; either keep a belt comment citing the loader's >=1 validation or restructure the guard.

warnings.title: E6 guard trusts a non-core auto-follow actor: the app skips the follow-up while the QoS editor is open, and any command source that omits it strands never-drop classes on zero lanes
warnings.detail: validate_set_lane predicts the settled weights assuming the app's auto-follow write; core never writes them. The app suppresses the follow-up when qos_mode_manual sees the editor open (keyboard lane keys bypass the panel's zeroed-lane skip), and any other command source that omits the follow-up gets the bus's blessing for a never-drop class parked on a zero-weight lane — backstopped only by the E6 flow floor. The coupling is proven by this very PR: 3 demos + 2 test fixtures had to be retrofitted to mirror the app (sla_weights' comment documents the must-mirror rule). Correction during verification: pre-diff the bus did NOT reject these edits either (untouched pipes were [1,1,1], all lanes nonzero) — the zero-lane exposure is new but MVP-unreachable: email (30%) and streaming (10%) are both droppable, no max_loss_pct==0 class exists.
warnings.recommended_fix: Make the auto-follow a core-side effect of applying Cmd_Set_Lane (or an atomic composite command) so the invariant the guard assumes is enforced where state changes; or mirror the panel's zeroed-lane skip in the keyboard path and document the contract.

warnings.title: Stale 'documented-as-canon' comments survive the fix — the exact drift class this PR's root cause blames
warnings.location: data/balance.json:2 (lane_presets clause), core/topology.odin:35, core/serialize.odin:66+332, core/qos.odin:51, core/determinism_test.odin:92, app/render/wire_path_test.odin:58
warnings.detail: The PR's root cause: the 5.8 drift was 'documented as canon' in balance.json. The rewritten _comment still says default_lane_preset is 'the resting position every pipe starts on + the E5 all-zero fallback' — both halves now false (pipes start on qos_unconfigured_weights; the E5 fallback is qos_unconfigured_weights, qos.odin:319). Five more comments still describe the balanced/default preset as the resting default. wire_path_test's fixture also omits auto_ladder, so its drawn pipes now carry inert {0,0,0} weights behind the stale comment (benign — nothing there reads weights; app render tests are outside the CI gates).
warnings.recommended_fix: Rewrite the default_lane_preset clause (manual quick-set default only) and the five code comments to name qos_unconfigured_weights as the resting + E5 default; give wire_test_catalog a real ladder row.

warnings.title: Committed spec artifact under-documents the change: validate_set_lane semantics, qos_auto_weights_after, and palcheck are absent from its code map/tasks; change log empty
warnings.detail: The spec self-reports status:done with all tasks [x], but has zero mentions of validate_set_lane (whose E6 semantics changed to settled weights), qos_auto_weights_after (new exported proc), or harness/palcheck.odin; its Spec Change Log section is empty; and its decision table says 'never-drop bus guard unchanged', contradicting the diff. The PR body documents all of this accurately — the durable in-repo record is the stale one.
warnings.recommended_fix: Add the guard rework, qos_auto_weights_after, and the palcheck oracle change to the spec's code map + tasks, fix the table row, fill the change log.

notes_list.title: Era-advance survival of the default lacks a dedicated unit pin (covered only via era_advance.dem golden replay)
notes_list.detail: AC3 names save/load + era advance + tier change. Tier has a dedicated test; save/load IS pinned (test_qos_serialization_sparse_and_roundtrip, qos_test.odin:209 — zero QoS bytes + identical hash); era advance is exercised only through the era_advance.dem replay gate (weights are untouched state; the demo replays green). A dedicated pin would survive demo churn.
notes_list.recommended_fix: Optional: add a white-box era-advance pin asserting {0,100,0} survives an era transition.

notes_list.title: Demos hardcode app-mirroring ladder splits — a playtest ladder re-tune silently desyncs demos from app behavior
notes_list.detail: The new `weights` directives restate ladder values (50/30/20, 70/30/0) that balance.json owns (ODN-5). A ladder re-tune re-blesses goldens against stale splits with no failure signal.
notes_list.recommended_fix: Consider a harness directive that lowers the ladder result (weights-auto <pipe>) instead of pinned integers.

notes_list.title: Panel never-drop cycle guard checks CURRENT weights while the bus now checks settled weights — panel under-offers legal lanes
notes_list.detail: The cycle skips zero-CURRENT-weight lanes for never-drop classes; the bus now accepts those assignments on auto pipes (the auto-follow reserves them). On an untouched {0,100,0} pipe the cycle would offer only Standard though Express is assignable. MVP-unreachable (no never-drop classes yet).
notes_list.recommended_fix: When the pipe is auto (weights==qos_auto_weights), test the after-weights instead of stored weights in the cycle skip.

notes_list.title: assigned-flag is sticky: reverting every lane to Standard keeps override entries, so the never-drop fold stays engaged
notes_list.detail: apply_set_lane replaces entries in place — a revert to Standard keeps the (pipe,class) entry, so `assigned` stays true. MVP-invisible (droppable-only, defaults Standard → {0,100,0} either way); with a future never-drop class defaulting off Standard, a fully-reverted pipe holds {70,30,0} rather than {0,100,0} — arguably correct safety, worth pinning as intended.
notes_list.recommended_fix: Pin the reverted-pipe ladder result in a test once never-drop content lands (or document the sticky-engagement as intended).

notes_list.title: Defensive fallback branches re-sourced to qos_unconfigured_weights but unpinned (both unreachable via the bus)
notes_list.detail: The out-of-range resting fallback and the E5 all-zero default_w wiring read the helper but no test pins either branch (unreachable via the command bus).
notes_list.recommended_fix: Optional white-box pins: stale-slot call; pipe_weights={0,0,0} then assert full-Standard caps.

notes_list.title: default_preset_idx is now write-only config (loader-only writes, no production reader)
notes_list.detail: This PR removed the last core consumers; only the loader + tests reference it. Its comment still claims an app-side role the app doesn't perform.
notes_list.recommended_fix: Either give the panel a default-chip highlight (its documented role) or retire the field with the next balance.json version bump.
